title: A first collaboration conversation with Hunter's Hope Foundation

sentences.text: At Cure and Action for Tay-Sachs (CATS) Foundation, we support Tay-Sachs families; Hunter's Hope Foundation supports families affected by Krabbe disease.
Both diseases involve missing enzyme activity in cells’ recycling compartments, making shared research approaches worth exploring—not assuming.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: A Natural History Study of the Gangliosidoses and Registry Gangliosidoses already include Tay-Sachs.
We propose comparing their approaches to collecting information, rather than assuming they can be used unchanged for Krabbe.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Tay-Sachs involves GM2 buildup; in Krabbe, damage from psychosine buildup is described as a hypothesis.

Please help check whether GM2 buildup, loss of developmental and movement skills, and a cherry-red spot at the back of the eye also occur in Krabbe, rather than treating missing records as proof of absence.
Before joining forces, we should also review the approval-status and gene-variant questions below with appropriate experts.
This month, we propose sending Hunter's Hope one focused inquiry: could The Natural History of Infantile Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy include people with HEXA-related disorders (Tay-Sachs disease)?
The shared enzyme-deficiency biology motivates this question, but does not establish eligibility.
Can we verify the reported approval gap—no approved disease-modifying therapy for Tay-Sachs, CLN3 disease or Krabbe, versus nine of twelve related diseases—and understand why?

Which GBA1, HEXA, NPC1 and GAA variants might respond to a protein-stabilizing chaperone, and could they be classified like GLA variants in published migalastat evidence for discussion with a neurologist?
I am writing on behalf of CATS to explore a modest collaboration.
Tay-Sachs and Krabbe share underlying enzyme-deficiency biology.
Could you help us ask whether The Natural History of Infantile Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy could include Tay-Sachs?
We would welcome your guidance on what needs checking first.
[Your name], on behalf of Cure and Action for Tay-Sachs (CATS) Foundation
